parts.title: Getting a job with an airline
parts.formTitle: Getting a job with an airline
parts.transcript: IELTS Listening, version 572.62. Section 1: a young woman (Ellie) phones a friend (Greg) who works for an airline (Eurontas) about a cabin crew attendant job. Duties: safety demonstration, dealing with money from sales, serving food. Requirements: over 19, at least 168 cm, English and maths, another language desirable, must be able to swim. Training: what to do in case of illness during a flight; awareness of different cultures. Download application from website; mention experience dealing with supermarket customer queries and voluntary work in a team. Don't have to buy a uniform.

parts.transcript: Section 2: Marie Cooper talks about hospitality industry scholarships in Scotland. Scholarships are for people working full time who have at least three years' experience, with or without qualifications. The Scottish hospitality industry is very important to the economy (10% depend on it) and is highly regarded by visitors. Marie started at the Rock Hotel for flexible hours fitting a young family; the application needed a report on her workplace; the other winners were younger than she expected; at the Florida Beach Hotel all staff interact with guests; people only wanted to visit limited places (Edinburgh, St Andrews); she introduced a better customer feedback survey.
parts.instruction: You will hear a woman called Marie talking at a conference to a group of people who work in the hospitality industry in Scotland.

parts.transcript: Section 3: industrial design students John and Debbie discuss Education House, an eco-building. Diagram labels: Cooling Tower removes old/stale air (F); Weather Station checks temperature (G); Shower Tower pulls in fresh air (B); Tank reduces water temperature (H); Balcony uses rainwater for plants (E); Windows reduce heat loss (C). They find the entrance (behind a cafe via a shopping arcade) surprising; the productivity findings are predictable; they're amazed by the 'edge space' (surprising design); and staff reaction may be a problem for the recycled-water system.

parts.title: Textiles with Business Studies
parts.transcript: Section 4: University Open Day talk on the Textiles with Business Studies course. Now possible to work with the Engineering Faculty. Three areas: knitted, printed, woven. Work placement focuses on the global market. Year One: visual research with documentation. Year Two: optional traditional design processes module; students offered tutorials to help decide between the 3- and 4-year course. Year Three: reflective practice; students produce a dissertation, a portfolio and a business plan. Careers: stylists, retail managers, plus journalism and trend forecasting. Come back tomorrow for a short interview.
